source_name: ČOI – Česká obchodní inspekce (official site, incl. English mirror)
why_relevant: Consumer-protection inspectorate under MPO; supervises consumer-credit provision/intermediation where ČNB does not, and merchant compliance with payment-card acceptance duties (an explicit ÚOHS cooperation partner on IFR enforcement).

source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Sbírka rozhodnutí (Financial Arbitrator decision collection)
why_relevant: Statutory ADR body for payment-services and consumer-credit disputes; publishes full-text anonymised nálezy naming the institution — an authoritative, structured record of conduct expectations on card fraud liability, fees and payment execution.

source_name: Přehled dozorových orgánů na úseku ochrany spotřebitele (SOS – Asociace supervisor map)
why_relevant: NGO-maintained map of which Czech authority supervises which consumer-protection area; efficient snowball source for enumerating adjacent conduct regulators beyond ČNB.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí – finanční gramotnost portal: Dohled nad ochranou spotřebitele
why_relevant: Government-authored description of the split of consumer-protection supervision between ČNB, ČOI, finanční arbitr and others — useful to attribute a given deadline to the correct publisher.

source_name: ochranaudaju.cz – Czech data-protection professional news aggregator
why_relevant: Specialist secondary outlet republishing and interpreting ÚOOÚ outputs; useful as a change-detection tripwire and for context, not as a primary record.

source_name: Lupa.cz – ICT/regulatory trade press coverage of NIS2 and Portál NÚKIB
why_relevant: Reveals indirectly how the NIS2 registration machinery actually behaves in practice (portal defects, low compliance rates) — friction signals that formal regulator pages do not disclose.

source_name: Finmag.cz – reporting on NIS2 registration shortfalls and NÚKIB remediation guidance
why_relevant: Financial-sector-facing press that carries NÚKIB statements on missed registration deadlines and sanction exposure — useful early-warning of enforcement posture.

source_name: Big-four / law-firm NIS2 and ZKB compliance trackers (EY CZ, Proxima Legal, CQS, vseonis2.cz, umimenis2.cz)
why_relevant: Advisory-sector trackers consolidate obligations, transition periods and sanction ceilings into deadline tables; fastest way to see how the market interprets NIS2 duties for financial entities, and who is selling into that compliance spend.

source_name: ČBA — Bankovní regulace (topic hub)
why_relevant: Dedicated ČBA topic page explaining and tracking banking regulation — the association's own framing of rules issued by authorised bodies. Useful as a stable landing page whose linked articles carry the industry commentary on new/expected regulation.

source_name: ČBA — Kodexy a standardy (codes & standards)
why_relevant: ČBA is the author of binding-by-commitment sector standards and codes (self-regulation). These are quasi-regulatory instruments with their own effective dates and are the concrete industry response to EU/CZ rules. Directly relevant to A3 deadlines and to payments (open banking, client mobility, bank identity).

source_name: ČBA — Komise a pracovní skupiny (commissions & working groups)
why_relevant: Maps the internal expert commissions/sub-commissions/working groups staffed by member banks (legislation, payments, AML, etc.). This is the actor map of who drafts ČBA positions — high-value pointer for identifying named experts, topic ownership and where a given consultation response originates.

source_name: ČBA — Kalendář akcí (regulatory/event calendar)
why_relevant: The association's own event calendar — conferences, seminars and briefings are typically scheduled around regulatory milestones (transposition deadlines, ČNB/MF consultations). Cheap forward-looking signal for A3 deadlines.

source_name: ČBA — Pro média / tiskové zprávy (press room)
why_relevant: Press releases are where ČBA publicly criticises or welcomes draft legislation (e.g. bank tax, consumer credit, payments) and where dates and named spokespeople appear. Fastest-moving ČBA channel for regulatory reaction.

source_name: ČBA Monitor
why_relevant: Separate ČBA-run analytical/monitoring property linked from the main site. Likely carries sector data and commentary that contextualises regulatory impact; worth profiling as its own feed rather than assuming it duplicates cbaonline.cz.

source_name: ČBA — legacy/parallel domain czech-ba.cz (incl. EN 'About CBA')
why_relevant: A second ČBA domain still surfacing live sections (e.g. /cs/o-cba/komise-pracovni-organy, /en/about-cba) and cited by ČNB as the association's official URL. May hold archived documents no longer on cbaonline.cz — valuable for historical position papers.

source_name: ČBA Educa / cbaeducaplus.cz — odborné semináře
why_relevant: ČBA's training arm. Seminar titles and agendas (e.g. AML seminars with the regulator's view) are a leading indicator of which regulatory changes banks are being prepared for and on what timeline; speaker lists name ČNB/MF officials and bank compliance leads.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — bankovnikarty.cz
why_relevant: The card-industry association for CZ (founded 1991 as Mezibankovní sdružení pro platební karty). Describes itself as a sector platform covering technology, security, LEGISLATION and regulation, statistics and member education; issues Security Rules for cardholders and runs the 'Port of Security' conference. Core cell actor for card/payments regulation.

source_name: SBK — Aktuality (news/press archive subdomain)
why_relevant: SBK's running news archive, carrying member and scheme press releases (Mastercard, Visa) as recently as August 2026. Useful for dated card-scheme and card-regulation announcements aggregated in one Czech-language place.

source_name: SBK — Statistiky karetního trhu
why_relevant: Aggregated CZ card-market statistics (ATM withdrawals, cashless transactions, e-commerce transactions, volumes, card counts). Not regulation per se, but the denominator for assessing the impact/urgency of card regulation and for sizing the regulated population.

source_name: ČLFA — Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (main site)
why_relevant: 35 members covering ~86% of non-bank business financing, ~83% of non-bank consumer financing and ~95% of factoring in CZ. Actively co-drafts legislation on consumer credit/leasing and publicly comments on transposition timing (e.g. CCD2 in the consumer credit act amendment approved by government 16 Mar 2026, with ČLFA warning about the Nov 2026 effective date). Strong A3 deadline signal.

source_name: ČLFA — Stanoviska ČLFA (position papers)
why_relevant: The association's formal positions library: statements to government, joint memoranda (e.g. joint memorandum on CCD dated 3 Dec 2021), guidance on credit moratoria, vehicle return after lease termination, disclosure obligations. Directly the A3 'position paper / consultation response' artefact type, as PDF/DOC with dates.

source_name: ČLFA — Členské společnosti (member directory)
why_relevant: Directory of the ~35 member firms; combined with the stated market-share figures it defines the non-bank regulated population addressed by consumer-credit/leasing regulation. Feeds entity resolution for other workstreams.

source_name: AKAT ČR — Asociace pro kapitálový trh (main site)
why_relevant: Capital-market/collective-investment association (2008 merger of AFAM ČR and AKAT). Site is unusually well structured for A3: separate sections for laws & decrees, association documents, EFAMA documents, press releases, news, event calendar and member list — i.e. one hub covering rules, positions, deadlines and the regulated population.

source_name: AKAT ČR — Dokumenty AKAT (association documents / standards / positions)
why_relevant: Verified to contain dated association artefacts: strategy 2026-2030 (30 Mar 2026), fund classification methodology (Jun 2024, with the prior version's validity end date given), best-interest-of-client standards for investment services (Jun 2024), a ČNB reply on distribution rules (Mar 2022), and an association position on dividend payments (Jan 2022). RSS feed offered.

source_name: AKAT ČR — Dokumenty EFAMA (EU-level positions relayed to CZ)
why_relevant: AKAT republishes EFAMA (European Fund and Asset Management Association) material for Czech members. This is the mechanism by which EU-level consultation responses reach the CZ industry — useful for linking EU consultations to the domestic reading, and an English-language entry point in an otherwise cs cell.

source_name: ODOK / VeKLEP — eKLEP pro veřejnost (inter-ministerial comment procedure)
why_relevant: The government legislative portal where draft laws pass through 'meziresortní připomínkové řízení'. Association comments (ČBA, ČLFA, AKAT, ČEFTAS via Hospodářská komora or as připomínková místa) end up here as vypořádání tables — the single best place to see an association's actual, dated, itemised objections to a draft, which no association page reproduces in full.
